claims_and_derivations.claim: Octupole deformation beta_3 and transition operator M(E3) are rank-3 parity-odd spherical tensors, giving transition rates B(E3) in e^2 fm^6. Quadrupole cubic invariant q3 = -sqrt(7/2) <(Q2 x Q2)_2 . Q2> = <Q^3 cos 3gamma> is a rank-0 parity-even scalar invariant formed entirely from quadrupole operators, with charge-length units e^3 fm^6, not energy. The operator-level distinction does not imply dynamical decoupling of quadrupole/octupole sectors or require beta3=0; in coupled states q3 evolves through wavefunction changes. Diagonal expectation values of M(E3) in good-parity laboratory stationary states vanish identically.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Cline 1986 p. 687; BM-II Chapter 4; manuscript Eqs.(3-7-q3-def)-(3-7-E3-diag-zero)
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Exact operator definitions; parity conservation in strong/EM Hamiltonian.

claims_and_derivations.claim: When j_p, j_n, R act on mutually independent tensor product factor spaces, they commute, so the scalar triple product chi_geom = j_p . (j_n x R) is already Hermitian without additional symmetrization. Because all angular momenta are axial vectors, chi_geom is strictly P-even and T-odd, invariant under proper rotations SO(3). Under an orthogonal spatial reflection across a plane, axial vectors transform with det(M_axial) = +1, so ordinary spatial reflection does not reverse chi_geom; this handedness is not a parity-odd order parameter. Invariance of chi_geom does not prove the whole oriented state is reflection invariant. T alone also reverses chi_geom; C = T R_y(pi) is the standard convenient body-fixed chiral operation, not the unique possible sign-reversing transformation.
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Three angular momentum operators in disjoint tensor spaces; pure axial vector kinematics.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Standard nuclear chirality transformation C = T R_y(pi) acts on body angular momentum components as J1 -> J1, J2 -> -J2, J3 -> J3. C is anti-unitary; its eigenvalues are phase-dependent and cannot serve as good +/- chiral parity labels. For integer spin I (even fermion number), T^2 = +1 and R_y(pi)^2 = +1; for half-integer spin I (odd fermion number), T^2 = -1 and R_y(pi)^2 = -1; in both cases C^2 = T^2 R_y(pi)^2 = (-1)^(4I) = +1. C^2 = +1 does not protect Kramers degeneracy. In nuclei with both octupole and chiral rotation, the collective potential energy surface does not necessarily form 4 isolated physical wells. Parity projector P^+- defines mutually orthogonal subspaces (P+ P- = 0), but does not guarantee fourfold near-degeneracy (Delta E+ != Delta E-).
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Anti-unitary quantum mechanics; multi-dimensional non-separable potential surfaces.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Delta l = Delta j = 3 is a common and strong coherent driver of octupole collectivity, but not mathematically strictly necessary; E3 allows Delta l = 1, 3 and Delta j <= 3 under parity and triangle selection rules. Near Z approx 56, N approx 88 (e.g. Ba, Ce), driving pairs are proton pi(d_5/2 - h_11/2) and neutron nu(f_7/2 - i_13/2). In actinides near Z approx 88, N approx 134-136 (e.g. 224Ra), driving pairs are proton pi(f_7/2 - i_13/2) and neutron nu(g_9/2 - j_15/2). The Ba pairs must not be applied to Ra.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Butler & Nazarewicz 1996 RMP 68, 349 PDF p. 5 (journal p. 353); manuscript Eqs.(3-7-delta-lj)-(3-7-favored-octupole)
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Spherical shell model single-particle levels near Fermi surface.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Multi-step Coulomb excitation in 146Ba (Bucher et al. 2017) directly measured ground-state E3 RME <3_1^-||M(E3)||0_1^+> = 0.65(+14/-20) e b^(3/2) and B(E3; 3^- -> 0^+) = 48(+21/-29) W.u., confirming strong octupole collectivity. E1 matrix elements largely rely on prior tau/BR data. D_0 = D_0^macro + D_0^micro is a phenomenological liquid-drop + shell decomposition convention. SCCM calculation specifically compares neutron and proton contributions (neutron high-j low-K occupancy cancellation). Macro and micro terms do not universally have opposite signs. Strong E3 does not alone prove a rigid static pear shape.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Bucher 2017 PRL 118, 152504 PDF pp. 2–5, Table I, Figs. 3–5; manuscript Sec. 3.7.5.1
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Multi-step Coulomb excitation with GRETINA and CHICO2; GOSIA analysis.

claims_and_derivations.claim: In a single transition connecting states of opposite parity, lowest allowed multipole mixing is E1 + M2 (Delta pi = -1); E1 + M1 or E1 + E2 mixing in a single transition is strictly forbidden by parity. Energy overlap of E1 with M1/E2 is an unresolved experimental doublet. Under strong-coupling single-K rotor models, ratio is B(E1; I -> I-1) / B(E2; I -> I-2) = (12/5) (D0^2 / Q0^2) (CG_1^2 / CG_2^2), where 12/5 = (3/(4pi)) / (5/(16pi)). Extracting |D0| requires independent Q0 from same-nucleus intraband B(E2)/Qt or model mapping. When lacking lifetime and CoulEx/absolute RME data, branching ratios alone give only |D0/Q0|.
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Axially symmetric single-K rotor limit; parity conservation in EM transitions.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Comprehensive spectroscopic evaluation requires: (1) quartet level scheme; (2) intra-band E2, interband M1/E2 between chiral partners, and alternating E1 between parity partners; (3) independent E3 collectivity constraints. In 78Br and 74As, current experimental data provide candidate chiral-parity structures, but lack complete lifetime and B(E3) precision to establish rigid quartets; detailed data and potential surfaces are deferred to Section 4.5.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Liu 2016 PRL 116, 112501; Liu Chen 2016 thesis; Xiao Xiao 2019 thesis; manuscript Sec. 3.7.5.3
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Data limitations in transitional A approx 70–80 nuclei.
